# Issue #2078: Driver: a merge whose lowered files conflict is re-lowered by the compiler built from the merged sources, not the old binary

[Open and answer this issue on GitHub](https://github.com/Nikaia-Foundation/Nikaia/issues/2078).

`ready` · opened 2026-11-18 · updated 2026-11-18 · 0 comments

Found while: running the performance lane's driver (Benchmarks Game, #1611), 2026-11-18. Related: #1430 (re-lowering a conflicted merge), #1333 (regenerating a clean merge), #1916 (the tree worktree).

## Probe

When the driver merges `origin/develop` before the next issue, the merge conflicts in `crates/nikaia-std/src/compiler/lowered.rs`. Develop has added a new method, `NodeId::at`, which `tree_build.nika` calls. The driver aborts:

```
error[NK1171]: `node_id::NodeId` has no method called `at`.
    --> target/ledger-tree/crates/nikaia-std/src/compiler/tree_build.nika:154:9
ESCALATE drive: merging origin/develop before the next issue, merge conflicted in crates/nikaia-std/src/compiler/lowered.rs, re-lowering failed (lower-std before the build), merge aborted (drive.nika ce846b53)
```

Resolving the merge by hand in this order worked (commit 208ef57f):

1. Take their `lowered.rs`.
2. Remove one stale import (E0432).
3. `cargo build --profile fast -p nikaia`.
4. `lower-std` with the **new** binary.
5. Build again.

## Cause

`scripts/drive.nika`, `drive_merge_regenerate`, the block after `let first = ... {build}`. When the first build of the merged tree fails, the driver runs LOWER (`drive_merge_lower`) with the binary from before the merge. That compiler only knows the declarations of the old side. So it refuses every `.nika` file that uses something develop newly declared (NK1171), and the merge is aborted.

The first build usually fails for a small reason in the taken lowered files, such as a stale `use`, a missing field, or the digest. The old binary cannot fix those, because it cannot lower the new sources at all.

## Done when

The driver merges a develop that adds a method used by a lowered `.nika` file, with a conflict only in `lowered.rs`, and needs no hand work. The log shows `MERGE <sha8> re-lowered crates/nikaia-std/src/compiler/lowered.rs`, and the short checks are green.

## To build

1. In `drive_merge_regenerate`, when the first BUILD fails, do not reach straight for the old binary's LOWER. First try to make the merged sources build:
   - Write the **old** binary's lowering only for the files whose `.nika` side is unchanged by the merge.
   - Or, preferably, bootstrap the compiler without the lowered std. Check whether `lower-std` has or can get a mode that needs only the Rust parts.
   - Decide which of the two in the build and note it in the comment. If neither is possible without a new compiler feature, report it as `blocked`.
2. Keep the old binary as the last fallback only, and say in the ESCALATE text which step failed, e.g. `lower-std with the binary from before the merge refused <file>: <first error>`.
3. Add a `.nika` test (tests/compiler/tests/ or the driver's script tests) that recreates a lowered-only conflict, with a new method on their side, and expects the merge to settle.
4. Update the comment at the top of `scripts/drive.nika` (the #1430 paragraph) and the one on `drive_merge_regenerate`.

## Files

- `scripts/drive.nika` (`drive_merge_regenerate`, `drive_merge_lower`, `drive_merge_relower`)
- its test

# Issue #2088: Unobservable std tests: the Rust tests no program or test block can reach

[Open and answer this issue on GitHub](https://github.com/Nikaia-Foundation/Nikaia/issues/2088).

`blocked`, `bugs` · opened 2026-11-18 · updated 2026-11-19 · 14 comments

Filed by the driver from the `Found:` of the run of `issue-2082` (#2082) (owner, 2026-11-06). Title shortened by the supervisor (2026-11-19); the driver had set the Found line as the title.

## Decided (supervisor, 2026-11-19, by the owner's direction of 2026-11-18)

* No separate CI job for these tests, and no `test = false` while a `#[test]` is left in `nikaia-std` ("The std crate's Rust unit tests move into Nikaia, so nikaia-std has no cfg(test) build" (#2082)).
* Each test is sorted one by one in its sub-issue: what a program can observe becomes a program in `tests/compiler/tests/`; a pure branch becomes a `test` block (ADR-403 D3) of a function moved into `runtime/*.nika`.
* What only the crate's own Rust can reach is tested through the bridge of ADR-rust-boundary-1: "A package's Nikaia code and test blocks call the package's own Rust, described in contracts/crate.contracts" (#2233). Until that is built, those tests stay `#[test]` with a "Kept as Rust (#2082)" comment.
* `test = false` is set for `nikaia-std` once no `#[test]` is left; then the one-profile build (#2083).

Waits for #2233 and the open sub-issues.

## Found (the driver's original list)

no program or test block can reach these Rust tests, so they stay #[test]: build_time.rs (needs a step budget below the 10^10 default, comptime_run::Bounds, which no program sets); rt/exit.rs (the LEAVING flag of the at-exit allocator); rt/library.rs (thread reuse for C library _async calls, needs a C caller); either_text.rs (is_view is not observable); rt/worker.rs (I/O workers and the drain deadline); concat.rs tests 2-3 (buffer pointer reuse, as_ptr); count.rs test 3 (`of("text")` passes through, no emitter site writes count::of around text)

## Done when

Every sub-issue is closed, no `#[test]` is left in `crates/nikaia-std`, and #2082 can set `test = false`.

## Comments

### keywan-ghadami, [2026-11-18](https://github.com/Nikaia-Foundation/Nikaia/issues/2088#issuecomment-6971783640)

#### Decision paper (supervisor, 2026-11-18): the question goes to the owner

**Question.** Some hand-written `#[test]`s in `nikaia-std` check runtime internals that no Nikaia program and no test block can observe. What happens to them, so that `test = false` (the Decision of "The std crate's Rust unit tests move into Nikaia, so nikaia-std has no cfg(test) build", #2082) can hold?

**Affected so far** (from the run of #2082; about 236 tests in 28 files are not probed yet, so the list may grow):
* build_time.rs: needs a step budget below 10^10 (`comptime_run::Bounds`).
* rt/exit.rs: the LEAVING flag.
* rt/library.rs: thread reuse for C `_async` calls.
* either_text.rs: `is_view`.
* rt/worker.rs: the I/O workers and the drain deadline.
* concat.rs tests 2-3: pointer reuse.
* count.rs test 3: `of("text")`.

**Options**
* **a) A std test hook.** These tests become plain functions without `#[test]` and `cfg(test)`. They are registered with the dispatcher that `nikaia test --std` already runs (the 94 lowered test blocks), so they are compiled into the release binary like those.
  * Gain: coverage stays, `test = false` holds, no second compile.
  * Cost: existing Rust test code is rewritten in Rust (no new behaviour), and the binary grows a little.
  * Each one leaves when its code moves into Nikaia (#125).
* **b) Keep them as `#[test]`.** The `cfg(test)` build of all of nikaia-std stays. #2082's goal fails for the largest crate.
* **c) Delete them.** Real behaviour loses its check, such as the drain deadline and the at-exit flag.

**Recommendation: a).** It is the only option that keeps both the coverage and the single compile. Before a test goes into the hook, the run checks whether a program does reach it after all. For example, build_time.rs could be reached if a budget can be set.

**Until the owner decides**, #2082 continues with the 28 files not yet probed. Tests found unreachable stay `#[test]`; step 4 (`test = false`) waits for this decision.

# Issue #2117: std::thread::id() returns an opaque thread::Id (ADR-401)

[Open and answer this issue on GitHub](https://github.com/Nikaia-Foundation/Nikaia/issues/2117).

`blocked`, `ci` · opened 2026-11-18 · updated 2026-11-20 · 5 comments

Part of "Unobservable std tests" (#2088). Decided in ADR-401 (owner, 2026-11-18). Needed by "All tests in Nikaia…" (#2082) for `crates/nikaia-std/src/rt/library.rs`'s test `a_thread_is_kept_for_the_next_call`.

## What happens today

* `std` has no `thread` module; a Nikaia program cannot name the thread it runs on.
* `rt/library.rs:91-125` checks that a library's `_async` calls reuse an idle kept thread (ADR-284 D9) and that a busy one is not waited for, by comparing Rust's `std::thread::current().id()`.
* No test builds a Nikaia package as a C library and calls it from C; `tests/compiler/tests/a_package_built_as_a_rust_library_is_used_by_a_rust_crate.nika` is the pattern for a Rust caller.

## Decision (ADR-401)

* `std::thread::id() -> thread::Id`: an opaque id for the calling thread. `==`, `!=` and a hash (usable as a map key or set member); no arithmetic, no order, no conversion to a number.
* Inside: a process-wide counter, taken the first time a thread calls `id()` and kept for its life; never reused, not the OS id or an address. A thread that never asks costs nothing. It names a thread, not a task.
* `std::thread` holds nothing else.

## To build

1. The type `thread::Id` (equality and hash, nothing else) and a process-wide counter with a per-thread slot filled from it on the thread's first call to `id()`, not at thread start. Written as `.nika` where it can be; what has to stay Rust is listed in the report for "Self-hosting" (#557).
2. Part I: a short section on `std::thread` with `Id`, `id()` and ADR-401 D3's note on tasks.
3. `tests/compiler/tests/thread_id.nika`: `id()` twice on one thread is equal; a task started with its own thread (if Part II offers one) or a library thread gives an id that is not equal; an id as a map key finds its value. A compile-fail test (`.stderr`) shows that arithmetic on a `thread::Id` is refused.
4. A test that builds a package as a C library and calls its `_async` function from a small C program twice one after the other (same `id()`), then twice at once with the first one blocked (different `id()`). It replaces `a_thread_is_kept_for_the_next_call`; delete the Rust test. Where no C compiler is found the builder reports it, never skips silently.

## Done when

* `thread::Id` and `thread::id()` exist, is in Part I, and the tests of steps 3 and 4 pass.
* The Rust test in `rt/library.rs` is gone.
* The commit of step 4 carries `Fixes`.

## Files and limits

* `std`'s `thread` module, `docs/specification/10-nikaia-light.md`, `tests/compiler/tests/`, `crates/nikaia-std/src/rt/library.rs` (only to delete the test).
* No sleep as a wait for a thread to be idle: wait on what the runtime says. No test time limit raised.

# Issue #2118: std's default restart policy supervisor::Backoff() is written in Nikaia, its tests too

[Open and answer this issue on GitHub](https://github.com/Nikaia-Foundation/Nikaia/issues/2118).

`blocked`, `ci` · opened 2026-11-18 · updated 2026-11-21 · 9 comments

Part of "Unobservable std tests" (#2088). Decided by the owner on 2026-11-18. "All tests in Nikaia…" (#2082) needs it for the two Backoff tests in `crates/nikaia-std/src/supervision.rs`.

Needs #2468

## What happens today

Read in the code (develop 87efc723):

* `std`'s default restart policy, `Backoff`, is Rust: `crates/nikaia-std/src/supervision.rs:380-460`. It covers the struct, `Default`, `pub fn Backoff()` and `impl Restart for Backoff`.
  * Numbers: `first_delay` 100 ms, doubling up to a `ceiling` of 30 s.
  * An attempt that ran `healthy` (60 s) starts a new cycle.
  * A cycle longer than `give_up_after` (300 s) escalates.
  * Jitter: an xorshift seeded from the clock takes up to a quarter off each delay.
* The trait it implements is already Nikaia. `Restart`, `Failures` and `Next` live in `crates/nikaia-std/src/supervisor.nika`.
* The emitter writes `nikaia_std::supervisor::Backoff()` where a child names no policy (`crates/nikaia-std/src/compiler/emit_core_args.nika:2538`).
* Its two tests stay Rust `#[test]`s, `the_default_policy_grows_and_gives_up` and `a_healthy_run_starts_a_new_cycle`, because a Nikaia program cannot call its `decide`. Through `supervisor::run`, its numbers show only after 60 s of uptime or 300 s of crashes. That is the comment at `supervision.rs:463`.

## Decision

`Backoff` moves into `supervisor.nika` as `supervisor::Backoff()`. A program can name it, read its fields and call `decide` with a `Failures` it writes by hand. The behaviour and the numbers stay as they are.

## To build

1. Write `Backoff` in `supervisor.nika`:
   * the struct with the public fields `first_delay`, `ceiling`, `healthy` and `give_up_after`, and the private cycle start and seed;

# Issue #2154: Driver merges: a lowered-only conflict costs about 30 minutes of re-lowering; cut the conflicts in lowered.rs and re-lower only what changed

[Open and answer this issue on GitHub](https://github.com/Nikaia-Foundation/Nikaia/issues/2154).

`lowering`, `performance`, `blocked`, `tooling` · opened 2026-11-18 · updated 2026-11-21 · 5 comments

Found while: supervising the yaml lane (YAML package, #928), 2026-11-18. Related: #2078 (the merge re-lowers with the old binary and fails), #1102 (rebase conflicts in lowered files), #1278 (lower-std cache key), #1581 (a cold lowering of the tools package takes 3–5 minutes).

## Probe

On 2026-11-18 the yaml driver merged `origin/develop` before pushing its tested commits, twice. Both merges conflicted only in `crates/nikaia-std/src/compiler/lowered.rs` (3915 lines, the index every lane's lowered change touches). Each one cost about 30 minutes of wall time before the push:

1. In the first merge, the old binary's `lower-std` refused the merged sources, because develop had changed code parameters to `&mut impl FnMut` (ADR-views-3 D17). That is the failure #2078 covers. The supervisor had to bootstrap by hand: build develop's compiler, then `lower-std --sysroot /home/user/Nikaia/crates`, then build again.
2. In the second merge (`MERGE cb513c37 re-lowered crates/nikaia-std/src/compiler/lowered.rs`), the driver's own re-lowering in `target/ledger-tree` ran about 30 minutes, with the short checks after it, before `PUSHED cb513c37`.

With several lanes pushing to `develop`, almost every merge conflicts in `lowered.rs`. That makes each lane's integration slow, and the owner paused the yaml lane for the day to bring the integration speed back up.

## Cause

- The generated lowered files (`compiler/lowered/*.rs`, 273 files, plus the index `lowered.rs`) are checked in. Every lane that changes any lowered `.nika` file rewrites lines in the one shared index, so concurrent lanes conflict there even when their `.nika` changes do not touch each other.
- The driver settles such a conflict by running a full `lower-std` (plus a build on each side) in the ledger tree. That run lowers far more than the files whose `.nika` source changed in the merge, and its cache is cold or keyed too coarsely (#1278).

## Done when

A merge of `origin/develop` whose only conflicts are in lowered files settles in the driver in a few minutes (measured: the time between the `MERGE <sha8>` line and `short checks`, logged by the driver), without hand work. The supervisor notes in `docs/tokenspeed.md` or the driver log how long the next three such merges took.

## To build

1. Measure first: log in `drive_merge_regenerate` how long each step takes (build, lower-std, build again), and record one real lowered-only merge as the baseline in this issue.
2. Cut the conflict surface of `lowered.rs`: see what each lane changes in it (module lines, digests, a list of entries?), and change the lowering so that the index changes only when a module is added or removed. One option is to move the per-file part, such as a digest, into each `lowered/<file>.rs`. Another is a `merge=ours` driver in `.gitattributes` for the index and the lowered files, so that git never stops on them and the driver always regenerates. Decide which of the two in the build and give the reason in the comment.
3. Re-lower only what the merge changed: lower just the `.nika` files whose source differs between the merge base and the merged tree, plus their dependants, instead of a full `lower-std`. If `lower-std` has no such mode, add one, written in Nikaia. This builds on the cache key of #1278.
4. Keep #2078's order: the compiler built from the merged sources lowers, and the old binary is the last fallback.
5. Update the header comment of `scripts/drive.nika` and `docs/supervisor.md` (the merge step) with the new cost.

# Issue #2176: The trace has no way to see memos that hand-written host Rust keeps of...

[Open and answer this issue on GitHub](https://github.com/Nikaia-Foundation/Nikaia/issues/2176).

`decision`, `bugs` · opened 2026-11-19 · updated 2026-11-19 · 0 comments

Filed by the driver from the `Found:` of the run of `issue-1278` (#1278) (owner, 2026-11-06).

## Found

The trace has no way to see memos that hand-written host Rust keeps of lowered results, so "no state outside the trace" (the issue's soundness condition) does not hold on develop e6d25eb1. traced: (1) `crates/nikaia/src/parser/mod.rs:372` `bounds_beside: std::sync::OnceLock<BoundsBeside>` on a shared `Parsed`. Whichever parallel per-file lowering walks it first fills it through lowered `bounds_frame::bounds_beside`, so those bits land in that thread's bitset, and every other file reuses the value without them. (2) `crates/nikaia/src/text_tiers.rs:148` `static METHODS: OnceLock<MethodIndex> = ...get_or_init(|| nikaia_std::compiler::ty::method_index(library))`, process-wide, filled once by lowered code. REMEMBERED` (constants computed by lowered code, reused by later files on the same worker thread), and `KNOWN` / `DEFAULTS` / `AHEAD` (lines 601-660). # Issue #2191: Joining tasks held in a list fails with NK1343

[Open and answer this issue on GitHub](https://github.com/Nikaia-Foundation/Nikaia/issues/2191).

`ready` · opened 2026-11-19 · updated 2026-11-19 · 0 comments

Found while drafting "The Rust tests of `fs.rs` move into Nikaia: programs that see file names, writes, mappings and roots" (not filed yet); its test 11 (`many_threads_reading_and_writing_at_once_each_get_their_own_answer`) joins with `tasks.drain()` and does not wait for this fix. Part of "Unobservable std tests" (#2088).

## What happens today

Run on the release binary of 2026-11-18 (develop 690857c2), from a scratch directory, with the shared checkout's `target/release/nikaia`. Command: `nikaia run join2.nika`.

```
fn main() throws {
    let mut tasks = []
    for t in 0..<2 { tasks.push(spawn fn { t }) }
    let mut total = 0
    for task in tasks { total += task.join() }
    println(f"total: {total}")
}
```

Expected (ADR-094 D4: the `for` lends each task, and joining takes it away, which is written `tasks.drain()`): a refusal by the checker at line 5, `NK1131` ("You can't give away `task` here: it is an element of `tasks`, which is only borrowed."), whose help names `tasks.drain()`; a task has no `.clone()`, so the help offers only the drain. Written with `for task in tasks.drain()`, the program prints:

```
total: 1
```

Actual:

```
error[NK1343]: Internal compiler error.
 5 |     for task in tasks { total += task.join() }
   = note: Rustc output: cannot move out of `*task` which is behind a shared reference.
```

Shapes run today:

* `for task in tasks.drain() { total += task.join() }` prints `total: 1` (and, with 8 tasks of 300 rounds of `fs::write` and `fs::read_to_string` each, `answers that came back right: 2400`).
* A list of a struct `Job { n: i64, tag: String }` walked with `for j in jobs { total += j.finish() }`, where `fn finish(self) -> i64`, prints `total: 3`; so does `finish(j)` with `fn finish(j: Job) -> i64` over a `Job { n: i64 }`. Neither is refused: a `Job` can be copied out of the view. A task cannot.

## Governing decision

ADR-094 D4: "`for x in xs { … }` iterates views of `xs`'s elements and leaves `xs` where it was ... Iteration that takes the elements away is written — `for x in xs.drain()`". `NK1131` is the refusal for giving away an element of a lent list (`check_core_a_lent_place_given_away`, its help: "take the elements out of `{list}` with `{list}.drain()`"). An internal compiler error is never the answer to a program the checker should refuse.

## Cause, traced

The lowered loop (`tasks.rs`, line 31, of the 8-task program):

```
for task in tasks.iter() { total += task.join().await?; }
```

`emit_stmt_for` (`crates/nikaia-std/src/compiler/emit_stmt.nika:1136`) writes `.iter()` for a `for` over a place that the checker did not put in `facts.owned_loops` (ADR-094 D4; only a name holding a sequence is handed over, ADR-293 D19, `check_core_stmt.nika:2243`). `FailingTask::<T, E>::join` (`crates/nikaia-std/src/task.rs`) takes `self`, so rustc refuses the move out of `&FailingTask`.

The checker lets it through: `check_core_a_lent_place_given_away` (`crates/nikaia-std/src/compiler/check_core_leaves.nika:151`) is reached for a value handed back (line 73) and for an argument passed to a parameter that owns it (line 103), not for the receiver of `join`, which takes its task. Suspected beyond that: whether every `std` method that takes its receiver (`join` of each task kind, `close` of a writer) misses `NK1131` the same way; the check that settles it is a probe per method over a lent list of that type, run before the fix.

## To build

1. `NK1131` for the receiver of `join` on an element of a lent list (and of every `std` method found by the check above to take its receiver), with the help naming `{list}.drain()` and no `.clone()` for a type that has none. The change is in `crates/nikaia-std/src/compiler/check_core_leaves.nika` and the place the checker reads a method's receiver (`check_core_method.nika` / `check_core_call_on.nika`), with `crates/nikaia-std/src/compiler/lowered/` as output.
2. Test `a_task_in_a_lent_list_is_joined_by_drain.nika` in `tests/compiler/tests/`: the probe above, with `.stderr` holding the `NK1131` refusal at line 5 and its help naming `tasks.drain()`. It fails on today's binary (`NK1343`).
3. Test `a_list_of_tasks_is_joined_in_a_drain_loop.nika`: the same program with `for task in tasks.drain()`, `.stdout` holding the row `total: 1`. It passes today and guards the way the help names.

## Done when

`nikaia test` gives the `NK1131` refusal of item 2 (no `NK1343`) and the row `total: 1` of item 3. One commit carries `Fixes` with the fix and both tests. The report has one `Found:` line per finding, one per `std` method the check finds missing `NK1131`.

## Files and limits

* `crates/nikaia-std/src/compiler/check_core_leaves.nika`, `check_core_method.nika` or `check_core_call_on.nika`, their lowered `.rs` as output, and the two tests with their `.stdout` / `.stderr`.
* No change to the lowering of `for` (ADR-094 D4 keeps it lending) and none to `crates/nikaia-std/src/task.rs`. No new Rust, no new `#[test]`.
* If the supervisor would rather have the loop hand the list over when the list is not read after it, that changes ADR-094 D4 and is a `decision` issue, not this build.

# Issue #2193: A number handed back where nothing is wanted reaches Rust as an internal compiler error (NK1343): `catch { -1 }` over a call without a result, and `return k` in a function without one

[Open and answer this issue on GitHub](https://github.com/Nikaia-Foundation/Nikaia/issues/2193).

`ready` · opened 2026-11-19 · updated 2026-11-19 · 0 comments

Found while drafting "The lock tests of std move into Nikaia programs" (#2189). No item of it waits for this: its race program (item 5) ends the handler with `catch { return }`, which works.

## What happens today

Binary: `target/release/nikaia` (nikaia 0.1.0, built 2026-11-18 06:16 from `develop`), run in a scratch directory outside the checkout with `nikaia run FILE`.

**1. A number literal as the replacement of a `catch` over a value of type `()`.** `SharedMut::set(…; after:)` has no result and throws `Overtaken` (std.contracts):

```nika
fn main() throws {
    let s: SharedMut[i64] = SharedMut(7)
    let late = s.set(9; after: 7) catch { -1 }
    println(f"{s.get()}")
}
```

```
error[NK1343]: Internal compiler error.
  --> ice.nika:3:43
   |
 3 |     let late = s.set(9; after: 7) catch { -1 }
   |                                           ^^^
   |
   = note: Rustc output: `match` arms have incompatible types.
   = help: This is a bug in Nikaia, not in your program: the checker accepted it, and Rust refused the code it became. Please report it, with this message, at https://github.com/Nikaia-Foundation/Nikaia/issues.
```

Exit 101. `catch { 3 }` gives the same. Every other replacement is refused as it should be:

* `catch { k }` with `let k: i64 = -1` gives NK1103, *This `catch` hands back `i64`, but the value it guards is `()`.*
* `catch { "no" }` gives the same NK1103 with `String`.
* `let late: i64 = s.set(9; after: 7) catch { -1 }` gives NK1103, *This value is `()`, but the `let` declares `i64`.*
* `s.set(9; after: 7) catch { println("overtaken") }` as a statement prints `9`.

So only a number literal slips through, and only where the guarded value is `()`. It is not the lock: a function of the program's own that throws and has no result gives the same NK1343 at the literal:

```nika
struct Bad { why: String }
impl Error for Bad { fn message(ref self) -> String { return self.why.clone() } }

fn check(n: i64) throws {
    if n > 5 {
        throw Bad { why: "big" }
    }
}

fn main() throws {
    let late = check(9) catch { -1 }
    println("done")
}
```

```
error[NK1343]: Internal compiler error.
   --> ice_own.nika:11:33
    |
 11 |     let late = check(9) catch { -1 }
    |                                 ^^^
    |
    = note: Rustc output: `match` arms have incompatible types.
```

**2. A value after `return` in a function without a result.**

```nika
fn nothing() {
    let k: i64 = 3
    return k
}

fn main() throws {
    nothing()
    println("done")
}
```

```
error[NK1343]: Internal compiler error.
  --> ret_var.nika:3:5
   |
 3 |     return k
   |     ^^^^^^^^
   |
   = note: Rustc output: mismatched types.
   = note: Try adding a return type.
   = help: This is a bug in Nikaia, not in your program: the checker accepted it, and Rust refused the code it became. Please report it, with this message, at https://github.com/Nikaia-Foundation/Nikaia/issues.
```

Exit 101. `return 3` and `return "x"` give the same.

No open issue names either shape (searched the titles for NK1343, `catch`, `return`).

## Expected

* Part I 7.1: "The block supplies the replacement value", and "The `catch` has the type of the value it guards". Part III C (NK1103): a `catch` whose block hands back a value of another type than the one it guards is refused. Shape 1 is NK1103, *This `catch` hands back `i64`, but the value it guards is `()`.*, as `catch { k }` already gets.
* Part III C (NK1104): a `return` that is not what was declared is refused. Shape 2 is NK1104 at the `return`.
* Part III C.1 and C.4: NK1343 is for what the checker could not foresee; neither shape is a valid program.

## Cause

Suspected, read off the code; item 1 checks it with a probe.

* Shape 1: `check_core_flow_try_catch` in `crates/nikaia-std/src/compiler/check_core_flow.nika` (around line 2007) accepts the handler when `value.fits(answers)`. A number literal takes the type it is asked for (Part I 2.4: not typed until a use types it), so the literal `-1` is suspected to come out as the guarded `()`, or as unknown, and to fit. `catch { k }`, whose type is fixed, reaches `expect_type` and is refused.
* Shape 2, traced: `check_core_returns` in `crates/nikaia-std/src/compiler/check_core_leaves.nika` (around line 894) starts the comparison with `let expected: Ty = state.expected?.clone() ?? return`. A function without a result has no `expected`, so a value after `return` is never asked.

## To build

1. Check the cause of shape 1: run `nikaia run scripts/where.nika -- check_core_flow_try_catch` and a probe that prints the handler's type for `catch { -1 }` and for `catch { k }` beside a guarded `()`. A cause shown false is answered `wrong I7: ...` in the report.
2. Refuse shape 1 with NK1103: a number literal ending a `catch` block over a guarded `()` is asked against `()` like any other value. Test: `tests/compiler/tests/a_catch_handing_back_a_number_over_nothing_is_refused.nika` with its `.stderr` (the NK1103 of the probe above, on `SharedMut::set(…; after:)` and on a function of the program's own that throws and has no result).
3. Refuse shape 2 with NK1104: in a function without a result, `return` with a value is refused, the help saying to drop the value or declare the result. Test: `tests/compiler/tests/a_return_with_a_value_in_a_function_without_a_result_is_refused.nika` with its `.stderr` (a variable, a number literal and a text literal, each in its own function).
4. Sweep for the rule (I10): every place that compares a value against an expected type and returns early when the expected type is missing or `()`. Name each one checked in the report; one that also lets a value through to rustc gets its case in the test of item 2 or 3.

## Done when

* Both probes above end with NK1103 and NK1104, exit 1, and no NK1343.
* The two tests are green at both settings, and failed on the unfixed tree.
* The commit of item 3 or 4, whichever is last, carries `Fixes #N` (#N being this issue's number); the others say `Part of #N`.
* The report gives a `Found:` line for each defect met on the way.

## Files and limits

* `crates/nikaia-std/src/compiler/check_core_flow.nika`, `crates/nikaia-std/src/compiler/check_core_leaves.nika`, and what item 4 names; their lowered `.rs` is output.
* `tests/compiler/tests/` (the two programs and their `.stderr`).
* No new Rust, no new Rust test, no new NK code (NK1103 and NK1104 exist).

## Ruled out

* The emitter of `catch`: it writes what the checker hands it. The fix is in the checker, which must refuse both shapes before emitting.
* `set(…; after:)` and the lock: the program's own `check` above fails the same way.

# Issue #2194: A number read from a lock is taken by a spawned task as if it moved (NK2101 on a `Seen[i64]`), and the help's `.clone()` then draws a warning that it makes nothing new (NK1350)

[Open and answer this issue on GitHub](https://github.com/Nikaia-Foundation/Nikaia/issues/2194).

`ready` · opened 2026-11-19 · updated 2026-11-19 · 0 comments

Found while drafting "The lock tests of std move into Nikaia programs" (#2189). No item of it is blocked: its race program (item 5) races two `set(…; after:)` calls on a literal witness. A program that used `n.get()` as the witness in two tasks, the natural way to write the race, meets this defect.

## What happens today

Binary: `target/release/nikaia` (nikaia 0.1.0, built 2026-11-18 06:16 from `develop`), run in a scratch directory outside the checkout with `nikaia run FILE`. The same message at `--user-parallelism no` (exit 1) and `yes` (exit 101; a refused program elsewhere, such as a missing method, exits 1 at `yes`, so that exit code is a second thing to look at in item 1).

```nika
fn main() throws {
    let n: SharedMut[i64] = SharedMut(0)
    let seen = n.get()
    let a = spawn fn { n.set(1; after: seen) catch { return } }
    let b = spawn fn { n.set(2; after: seen) catch { return } }
    a.join()
    b.join()
    println(f"{n.get()}")
}
```

```
error[NK2101]: You're using `seen` after a background task took it.
  --> seen.nika:5:24
   |
 5 |     let b = spawn fn { n.set(2; after: seen) catch { return } }
   |                        ^
   |
   = note: A task started with `spawn` may outlive this function, so it takes the variables it uses with it. `seen` is a `Seen[i64]`, so it went to the task.
   = note: Numbers, `bool`s, views and `Shared[T]` handles aren't taken: they're copied.
   = help: Make a copy before and hand over the copy: `let copy = seen.clone()`, then use `copy` inside.
1 value a task took with it
```

Exit 1 at the default setting. The message contradicts itself: its second note says numbers are copied, and `seen` is a number. Following the help:

```nika
fn main() throws {
    let n: SharedMut[i64] = SharedMut(0)
    let seen = n.get()
    let seen2 = seen.clone()
    println(f"{seen2}")
}
```

```
warning[NK1350]: `seen` is an `i64`, which copies by itself: `.clone()` makes nothing new.
  --> seen_clone.nika:4:17
   |
 4 |     let seen2 = seen.clone()
   |                 ^^^^^^^^^^^^
   |
   = note: A number, a `bool`, a `char` and a type whose every part copies are copied wherever they are read (ADR-294 D9.1).
   = help: Delete `.clone()`.
0
```

Variants, each run the same way:

* `let seen: i64 = n.get()` in the first program: accepted, prints `1`, exit 0.
* Two spawns that each run `println(f"{seen}")`, with no `set` at all: the same NK2101. So it is about the task, not the lock door.
* `async(detached)` in place of `spawn`: the same NK2101 ("after a detached task took it").
* Handing `seen` twice to `fn take(x: i64)` and putting it in two tuples, with no task: accepted, prints `1 1 0 0`.
* A `SharedMut[Vec[i64]]` read with `get` and used in two spawns: NK2101, rightly, since a `Vec` moves.

No open issue names it (searched the titles for `Seen` and task).

## Expected

* ADR-281 D22: `get` hands out `Seen[T]`, and the emitter erases the stamp: a `Seen[i64]` is an `i64` in the language below. D23: the stamp passes through what cannot write it back.
* ADR-294 D9.1, as NK1350 cites it: a number is copied wherever it is read. So a `Seen[i64]` is copied into each task, and the first program prints `1` or `2` (whichever `set` comes first; the other is overtaken).
* Part III C.1 and C.4: NK2101 stands in for rustc's "use of moved value". It is not asked of a value that copies.

## Cause

Traced in the code, not yet in a run; item 1 confirms it with a probe.

* `a_task_takes_these` (around line 175) and `takes_of_a_lambda` (around line 145) in `crates/nikaia-std/src/compiler/check_lambdas.nika` record a local as taken when `takes_away(world, local.ty)` holds.
* `takes_away` in `crates/nikaia-std/src/compiler/check_values.nika` (line 12) starts with `moves_away(ty)`.
* `moves_away` in `crates/nikaia-std/src/compiler/check_types.nika` (line 142): for a `Ty::Named` it is true unless the name is a number, `bool`, `char`, `scalar`, `Shared` or `SharedMut`. `Seen` is none of these, so `Seen[i64]` moves away. `copies_plainly` (line 162) has the same gap. Neither looks through the stamp with `Ty::unseen()` (`crates/nikaia-std/src/compiler/ty.nika`), as `Ty::fits` does.
* The note of NK2101 is built in `a_task_took_what_is_used_again` in `crates/nikaia-std/src/compiler/check_takes.nika` (around line 885) from `ty.shown()`, which is why it says `Seen[i64]`.

## To build

1. Confirm the cause: `nikaia run scripts/where.nika -- moves_away` and a probe that shows `moves_away` true for `Seen[i64]` and false for `i64`. A cause shown false is answered `wrong I7: ...` in the report.
2. Make `moves_away` and `copies_plainly` judge a stamped type by what it holds (`ty.unseen()`), so a `Seen[T]` moves exactly when `T` does. Test: `tests/compiler/tests/a_number_read_from_a_lock_is_copied_into_two_tasks.nika` with its `.stdout`: the first program above with `spawn`, a second pair with `async(detached)`, and a `bool` read with `get`; each prints its result, at both settings.
3. Keep the move of a stamped value that does move. Test: `tests/compiler/tests/a_list_read_from_a_lock_is_taken_by_the_first_task.nika` with its `.stderr`: a `Seen[Vec[i64]]` used in two spawns gives NK2101, its note naming the type.
4. Sweep for the rule (I10): the other callers of `moves_away` and `copies_plainly` (in `check_core_call_on.nika`, `check_core_flow.nika`, `check_core_leaves.nika`, `check_types.nika`, `check_values.nika` and `emit_exprs.nika`, 14 call sites) and any other test of a type's name that misses `Seen`. Name each one checked in the report; one that changes behaviour gets its case in the test of item 2.

## Done when

* The first program prints `1` or `2` and exits 0 at both settings, and `nikaia run` gives no NK2101 for the variants with a number or a `bool`.
* The tests of items 2 and 3 are green at both settings; the test of item 2 failed on the unfixed tree.
* The commit of item 4 carries `Fixes #N` (#N being this issue's number); the others say `Part of #N`.
* The report gives a `Found:` line for each defect met on the way.

## Files and limits

* `crates/nikaia-std/src/compiler/check_types.nika`, and what item 4 names; their lowered `.rs` is output.
* `tests/compiler/tests/` (the two programs and their `.stdout` / `.stderr`).
* No new Rust, no new Rust test, no new NK code.

## Ruled out

* The lock door: two spawns that only print `seen` fail the same way.
* The emitter: the checker refuses the program before anything is emitted.
* The message alone: the refusal itself is wrong, so changing the help without the check would still refuse a valid program.

# Issue #2195: A method called on a tuple or on `()` is refused as a type the compiler can't tell (NK1245), not as a method the type lacks (NK1171)

[Open and answer this issue on GitHub](https://github.com/Nikaia-Foundation/Nikaia/issues/2195).

`ready` · opened 2026-11-19 · updated 2026-11-19 · 0 comments

Found while drafting "The lock tests of std move into Nikaia programs" (#2189). No item of it waits for this: its programs use `set(…; after:)` under `catch`, as Part I 7.1 asks, and never call a method on the result. A reader who expects `set` to hand back a `Result` (and calls `.is_ok()` on it) meets this message instead of one that says what is wrong.

## What happens today

Binary: `target/release/nikaia` (nikaia 0.1.0, built 2026-11-18 06:16 from `develop`), run in a scratch directory outside the checkout with `nikaia run FILE`.

```nika
fn main() throws {
    let n: SharedMut[Vec[i64]] = SharedMut([0])
    let r = n.set([1]; after: [0])
    println(f"{r.is_ok()}")
}
```

```
error[NK1245]: The compiler can't tell what type `r.is_ok()` is.
  --> isok.nika:4:5
   |
 4 |     println(f"{r.is_ok()}")
   |     ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
   |
   = note: What is not known is not checked, so a type nothing can tell is refused rather than left to the language below.
   = help: Write the type down where the value is made, such as `let x: T = …`, or pass it to a parameter that declares one.
1 type error
```

Exit 1. The compiler does know the type of `r`: `set` hands back nothing, so `r` is `()`. The help asks for a type annotation, which cannot help.

The same NK1245, with nothing of the lock in it:

* `let r = n.set([1])` (a plain `set`): NK1245 on `r.is_ok()`.
* `fn noop() { let _x = 1 }`, then `let r = noop()` and `r.is_ok()`: NK1245.
* `let t = (1, 2)`, then `t.is_ok()`: NK1245 on `t.is_ok()`.

The same call on other types gives the right refusal:

* `let r: i64 = 3`, then `r.is_ok()`: `error[NK1210]: \`i64\` has no method called \`is_ok\`.`

# Issue #2198: Pipes, redirections and `&&` as a structure, not a shell text: a list of commands with their arguments and where each stream goes

[Open and answer this issue on GitHub](https://github.com/Nikaia-Foundation/Nikaia/issues/2198).

`note`, `safety` · opened 2026-11-19 · updated 2026-11-19 · 0 comments

Follows from "Decision: which shell `process::shell` runs on Windows" (#1937), owner, 2026-11-19, [ADR-raw-sinks-1](https://github.com/Nikaia-Foundation/Nikaia/blob/develop/docs/specification/adr/adr-raw-sinks-1.md) D9 item 3.

## Goal

What a program wants a shell for (a pipe `a | b`, a redirection `> file`, `&&` / `||`, a glob) is given later as a structure: a list of commands, each a program with its arguments, and where each stream goes. A value from outside is always one argument, so nothing is escaped and nothing has to be proved. It runs without a shell, the same on every platform. A sketch of the shape, not decided:

```nika
use std::process

let out = process::pipe([process::cmd("convert", [name, "-resize", "64x64", "-"]),
                         process::cmd("gzip", [])];
                        stdout: process::to_file("thumb.png.gz"))
```

A library that does hand a text to `sh` or `cmd.exe` is the shell library ADR-raw-sinks-1 keeps the `untrusted-shell` key for (D4, D5): its escaping is its own, and the application allows it.

## Open before it can be `ready`

* `std` or an official package (ADR-289 D2: is a pipeline an operating-system resource or a library on top of `process::run`?).
* The form of the structure, of `&&` / `||` and of a glob, written as an ADR.
* An argument that starts with `-` is not solved by this: "Decision: an outside argument that starts with `-` is read as an option" (#1939).

Status `note` until a program needs it; then it becomes a `decision` with a decision paper.

# Issue #2207: `nikaia bind js` writes the WebAssembly library's `.js` and `.d.ts`

[Open and answer this issue on GitHub](https://github.com/Nikaia-Foundation/Nikaia/issues/2207).

`targets`, `blocked` · opened 2026-11-19 · updated 2026-11-19 · 0 comments

## Goal

`nikaia bind js` writes the JavaScript binding of a library: the WebAssembly build's `<package>.js` and `<package>.d.ts` ([ADR-284](https://github.com/Nikaia-Language/Nikaia/blob/develop/docs/specification/adr/adr-284.md) D26, D28). This is the only part of "A binding is a generated file over the C library" (#112) that is not built. #112 is closed, and this issue carries the rest.

Found while tidying up "A library for other languages" (#88).
Needs #111

## Today

- `nikaia bind python`, `nikaia bind node` and `nikaia bind java` are built. `cli_commands_bind_refusal` in `crates/nikaia-std/src/compiler/cli_commands.nika` lets only these three through. For `js` it says: *`nikaia bind js` is not built: `python`, `node` and `java` are (ADR-284 D26, D28, D34). JavaScript in a browser is served by the WebAssembly build, which is not built yet.*
- The `.js` and `.d.ts` themselves come from the WebAssembly library: `target = "wasm32-unknown"` with `artifact = "c-library"` (D22, D23, D24). That generator is part of "A WebAssembly library is the same entry point on another target" (#111), which is not built and waits on "WebAssembly: where a parser's hash keys come from" (#276). `nikaia-std` does not build for `wasm32-unknown-unknown` today (`polling` refuses the target).

## Decision

ADR-284 D26: *`nikaia bind js` is D22's `.js` and `.d.ts`.* D28: JavaScript is served by the WebAssembly build; `nikaia bind node` stays the native shim for file and socket access. D29: a binding never widens what the library exports. No new decision is needed.

## To build

1. `cli_commands_bind_refusal` accepts `js`. `nikaia bind js` on a `c-library` package builds the package for `wasm32-unknown` and leaves `<package>.js` and `<package>.d.ts` beside the `.wasm` in `target/nikaia/c-library/`, carrying the ledger hash as the header does (D26). Whether this sets the target itself or refuses without `target = "wasm32-unknown"` is the builder's choice; the refusal, if chosen, names the setting.
   Test: `tests/compiler/tests/bind_js_writes_the_wasm_librarys_js_and_dts.nika` with `.stdout`, in the style of `bind_java_writes_a_class_per_handle_and_a_record_per_struct.nika`. It binds a small package and prints the exported names in the `.d.ts`.
2. `nikaia bind --help` and the refusal text in `cli_commands_bind_refusal` name `js` among the built languages.

## Done when

`nikaia bind js` on a `c-library` package writes `<package>.js` and `<package>.d.ts` with the package's entry points, and the test in item 1 shows them. The commit of item 1 carries `Fixes #N`. The report gives one `Found:` line per finding.

- `crates/nikaia-std/src/compiler/cli_commands.nika`, `crates/nikaia-std/src/compiler/project_drive.nika` (the `bind` dispatch), and their lowered files.
- Not touched: the `.js` generator itself, which #111 builds.

# Issue #2241: A block without `-> T` gets a row type the compiler writes from the row its grammar describes

[Open and answer this issue on GitHub](https://github.com/Nikaia-Foundation/Nikaia/issues/2241).

`language`, `libraries`, `blocked` · opened 2026-11-19 · updated 2026-11-19 · 0 comments

## Goal

A `dsl` block without `-> T` gets a row type the compiler writes from the `row` its grammar describes (ADR-323 D3, D5; ADR-299 D2, D22). `q.execute(db)` then hands back rows with fields: `u.name`, `u.a.id`. This comes after the declared-struct form "`dsl … -> T { … } eod`" (#477), by the owner's order of 2026-11-19: a program can read rows into its own struct first, and the type written from data comes last.

Part of #89
Needs #114
After #477

## Governing decisions

- [ADR-323](https://github.com/Nikaia-Foundation/Nikaia/blob/develop/docs/specification/adr/adr-323.md) D5: the grammar's entry returns `meta::Statement { row, parameters }`; a namespace is a field whose type is a `Record`. D3: `Text` is `String`, `Maybe(T)` is `T?`, `List(T)` is `Vec[T]`, `Record` a struct. D4: a message names the block and the grammar; `--comptime` prints the type.
- [ADR-299](https://github.com/Nikaia-Foundation/Nikaia/blob/develop/docs/specification/adr/adr-299.md) D22 (owner, 2026-11-19; it restates D12 and D13 without tables): the row is the record the grammar describes. A namespace's fields are reached through it (`u.a.id`). A field one level down is also reached by its own name (`u.name`) where nothing else in the row answers to that name; otherwise the short name is `NK1107`, and the help names the full paths. Deeper fields only by their full path. D14: the grammar refuses a name that cannot be a field.
- Not decided ([ADR-323](https://github.com/Nikaia-Foundation/Nikaia/blob/develop/docs/specification/adr/adr-323.md) §6): whether two blocks with the same columns share one type. Until it is: each block its own type.

## Today

After #114, a statement block's `execute` hands back `Vec[db::Row]`, and `--comptime` shows the row and parameter types the grammar described. No row type is written. The conversion of a `db::Row` into a typed row and `db::NullInField` (`packages/db/src/main.nika`) are not used by the compiler.

## To build

1. **The row struct.** For a statement block without `-> T`, write a struct from the described `row`: one nested struct per namespace (a field whose type is a `Record`), and the short names one level down by D22's rule. `execute` returns `Vec[<that struct>]`. Each block gets its own type.
   Test: `tests/compiler/tests/a_blocks_rows_have_its_columns_as_fields.nika` with `.stdout`. A stub grammar describes namespaces `a { id: I64, name: Text, email: Maybe(Text) }` and `b { id: I64 }`. A fake connection returns rows, and the program reads `u.name`, `u.email ?? "-"`, `u.a.id`, `u.b.id`.
2. **The conversion** (ADR-299 D8, D18). Each `db::Row` becomes the struct. A `Null` in a field that is not `T?` fails `execute` with `db::NullInField`, naming the field and the column.
   Test: `tests/compiler/tests/a_null_in_a_field_that_is_no_option_fails_execute.nika` with `.stdout`.
3. **The messages** (D22, ADR-323 D4). `u.id` where `a` and `b` both have `id` is `NK1107`, with help naming `u.a.id` and `u.b.id`. `u.emial` is `NK1107`, naming the block's line and the fields. A field two levels down read by its short name is `NK1107`, naming its full path.
   Test: `tests/compiler/tests/a_shared_or_misspelled_column_names_the_ways.nika` with `.stderr`.
4. **`--comptime` prints the written row type** of each block, beside #114's description.

## Done when

`for u in q.execute(db) { println(u.name) }` builds and runs on a statement block without `-> T`. `u.id` over two namespaces with `id` is `NK1107`, and the help names both paths. The commit of item 3 carries `Fixes #N`. The report gives one `Found:` line per finding.

## Files

The emitter's statement path that #114 adds, `check_fields.nika` (field access on the written type), `project_check.nika` (item 4), and their lowered files. Not touched: `packages/db`, #477's `-> T` path.

# Issue #2245: A grammar naming a rule it does not have is refused as a compiler bug (`NK1178`), not as the program's mistake

[Open and answer this issue on GitHub](https://github.com/Nikaia-Foundation/Nikaia/issues/2245).

`language`, `ready` · opened 2026-11-19 · updated 2026-11-19 · 0 comments

## What happens

A grammar that names a rule which neither the grammar declares nor Part II 10.8 offers as a built-in is not refused by the checker. The name reaches the generated parser, and the backend refuses it there.

- Where the grammar runs while the program is built (`dsl G { … } eod`, a `comptime`), the user gets `NK1178` with *This is a bug in the compiler, not in your program* and the backend's `Undefined rule`.
- Where it runs with the program, the user gets the backend's `error: Undefined rule: 'nmae'.`, without a code.

A rule called with values is refused properly (`NK1171`). The same misspelling without values is not.

Found while "A grammar declares a statement's columns and parameters" (#114) was being rewritten (a probe with `alpha`, which is no built-in; `alpha1` is).

## Probe

Run on `target/fast/nikaia` of `6c4b12ab`, in the shared checkout, with `nikaia check p.nika`:

```nika
grammar G {
    entry rule r -> String = s:nmae -> { s }
}

fn main() throws {
    let x = dsl G { abc } eod
    println(x)
}
```

**Expected** (the checker, before any parser is generated, in the words `NK1171` already uses for a rule called with values):

```
error[NK1171]: Grammar `G` has no rule called `nmae`.
```

**Actual:**

```
error[NK1178]: The parser generated for `G::r` didn't compile.
   = note: This is a bug in the compiler, not in your program.
    error: Undefined rule: 'nmae'
```

Shapes run:
- `s:nmae`, `s:alpha` and `s:text(alpha+)` in a `dsl` block: all `NK1178` as above.
- `G::r("abc")` called at run time (no build-time run): `error: Undefined rule: 'nmae'.` from the backend, at the right line, no `NK` code.
- Working: `s:raw_ident` in its place builds and prints `abc`.
- Working: a rule called with values and misspelled, `v:piar(1)` beside `rule pair(a: i64)`, is `error[NK1171]: Grammar `G` has no rule called `piar`.`

## Governing decision

Part III's code table: `NK1171` is *a member a known head or receiver does not have*, and the checker already uses it for a grammar's rule called with values (`grammar_call` in `crates/nikaia-std/src/compiler/check_grammar.nika`). Part II 10.8 (*The Grammar's Vocabulary*) lists the built-ins. `NK1178` says the generated parser not compiling is *this compiler's defect*, which is the mismatch: the defect is in the program, and the compiler should say so in its own words.

## Cause

`suspected`: `reference_type` in `crates/nikaia-std/src/compiler/check_grammar.nika` returns `Ty::Unknown` for a `Pattern::Ref` that is no rule of the grammar and none of the built-ins it knows, and refuses nothing. Only `grammar_call` (a reference with values) refuses an unknown name. Check that settles it: a refusal in `reference_type`'s fall-through turns the probe into `NK1171`.

The list of built-ins `reference_type` knows is not the whole of Part II 10.8 (it types some, and lets others through as `Unknown`). So the refusal needs the full list of 10.8's names, not just the ones `reference_type` types.

## To build

1. A `Pattern::Ref` without values that names no rule of the grammar and no built-in of Part II 10.8 is `NK1171`: *Grammar `G` has no rule called `nmae`.* The help names the nearest rule or built-in where one is close (as `nearest_parameter` in `dsl.nika` does for parameters), else *Declare the rule, or use a built-in of Part II 10.8.* The list of built-ins is one list in `check_grammar.nika`, used by this check and by `reference_type`.
   Test: `tests/compiler/tests/grammar_an_unknown_rule_is_refused.nika` with `.stderr`, covering `s:nmae` (help: `name` declared beside it) and `s:text(alpha+)` (help: `alpha1`).
2. The grammars in the tree still build: `nikaia test` on `tests/compiler/tests/grammar_*.nika` and the packages with grammars (`json`, `yaml`, `logic`) shows no new refusal. A built-in the list misses is added to the list, not worked around.

## Done when

The probe is refused with `NK1171` naming `nmae`, by the checker, and no grammar in the tree is refused. The commit of item 1 carries `Fixes #N`. The report gives one `Found:` line per finding.

## Files

`crates/nikaia-std/src/compiler/check_grammar.nika` and its lowered file. Not touched: the emitter (`emit_grammar.nika`) and `NK1178`'s other cases.

[Open and answer this issue on GitHub](https://github.com/Nikaia-Foundation/Nikaia/issues/2275).

`decision`, `adr` · opened 2026-11-19 · updated 2026-11-20 · 0 comments

Part of #904
Needs #2274

## Goal

After the grammar, database, views and collections records, about 190 numbered records and a few topic records with a count (`regex-1`, `async-5`, …) remain. Each needs its topic before it can be consolidated (ADR-decision-records-v2 D2, D4), and the owner confirms the topics (#904).

## Governing decision

ADR-decision-records-v2 D1, D2, D4.

## Today

`ls docs/specification/adr/adr-[0-9]*.md | wc -l` gives 196 at commit 443a4f4b; the grammar and database issues take seven of them (177, 296, 299, 323, 339, 366, 388).

## To build

1. **The table**, in this issue's body (the issue is the record): every live record, the topic it joins (one to three words, the general one first, as `grammar-syntax`), grouped by the index sections. A record that covers several topics is split by decision, as ADR-296 was. A topic record with a count keeps its name until it is changed (`regex-1`, then `regex-v2`, D4) and is listed only where it shares a topic with a numbered record.
2. **The owner confirms** the table; changes go into the body.
3. **One issue per topic**, in the form of "The decisions on how a grammar is written live in one record, `ADR-grammar-syntax-v1`" (#2264), each `Needs` the one before, so they run in order.

## Done when

Every live record that is not a `-v` record has a confirmed topic in this issue's table, and each topic has its consolidation issue; this issue is closed by hand when the last one is filed.

## Files and limits

No file changes; the result is the table and the issues.

## What was ruled out

Consolidating whatever a change happens to touch, without a table: topics would be cut differently each time.

## The table (draft, 2026-11-20, waiting for the owner's confirmation)

Rule: ADR-decision-records-v2 D1 (name `ADR-<topic>-v<n>`, one to three
lowercase words, general word first), D2 (one live record per topic), D4
(a topic's records are consolidated into its next `-v` record when one of
them is changed). Topics already in use (README, *Topics in use*, plus the
count-named records) are reused where a record belongs there: "joins
existing". A count-named record gets a row only where a numbered record
joins its topic. A record spanning several topics is split by decision.

# Issue #2302: The compiler, scripts and packages pass the raw path sink check by proof, not trusted:

[Open and answer this issue on GitHub](https://github.com/Nikaia-Foundation/Nikaia/issues/2302).

`blocked`, `safety` · opened 2026-11-19 · updated 2026-11-21 · 12 comments

## What

The compiler (`crates/nikaia-std/src/compiler/*.nika`), `scripts/*.nika` and `examples/` / `packages/` pass the raw path sink check (NK1308, brought to develop behind warn by #2303) by proof, not by `trusted:` (ADR-raw-sinks-1 D13, D14, D15, D16; owner's decision on #2242, 2026-11-19): each site is looked at alone. A name from `fs::read_dir` is opened under `root.join(dir)`; a name from outside that must be one component is guarded with `path::is_component`; a relative path that must stay below a root with `path::is_below`; a temporary directory comes from `fs::scratch()`. What is the tool's job (`nikaia build FILE` opens the file it is given) is said once in the manifest by a D15 line with a comment, e.g. `untrusted-paths-read = ["args"]`, never `trusted:` at a site.

Part of #2242
Needs #2300
Needs #2303

Today: the NK1308 check of the local ref wip/issue-2242 (0254f60c3) reports 41 sites in the compiler, 52 in `scripts/`, 14 in `examples/` and `packages/`. At 57379dba7 `grep -c 'Root::Anywhere'` gives 203 in the compiler, 243 in `scripts/`, 18 in `examples/` and `packages/` (most are not reached by data from outside and stay unreported); `mktemp` 0 in the compiler, 11 in `scripts/`. Largest groups: `scripts/drive.nika` 20, `scripts/agent.nika` 11; in the compiler `project_drive.nika` (`project_run_dir_tests`, a `read_dir` name opened under `Anywhere`).

The read_dir shape:

```nika
for name in fs::read_dir(dir, fs::Root::Anywhere) {
    let src = fs::read_to_string(f"{dir}/{name}", fs::Root::Anywhere)
}
```

becomes

```nika
let tests = root.join(dir)
for name in fs::read_dir(".", tests) {
    let src = fs::read_to_string(name, tests)
}
```

## Governing decision

ADR-raw-sinks-1 D13, D14, D15, D16.2 (nikaia's own D15 line with a comment), D16.3 (what no form covers is reported, not written around).

## Done when

The NK1308 check of wip/issue-2242, run over the compiler, `scripts/` and `examples/` / `packages/`, reports no site that neither a proof (join, guard, scratch) nor a commented D15 line in the manifest covers; no `trusted:` is added anywhere; the D15 lines of `nikaia`'s manifest (and of each package that needs one) carry a comment naming why; the builds and the tests the changed files touch pass; the last step's commit carries `Fixes #THIS`. A `Found:` line per finding, one per site no form covers.

## To build

1. **The D15 line for `nikaia`** in its manifest (the builder finds which one `nikaia` reads its settings from; `nikaia.toml` at the top), with a comment: the paths the tool opens come from its command line. Test `tests/compiler/tests/a_manifest_allows_untrusted_paths_from_args_for_reading.nika`: a package with `untrusted-paths-read = ["args"]` reads a file named by `cli::args` and builds; the same with `stdin` as the source is still reported (needs the NK1308 check: the builder may leave this test to the check's issue and say so in the report).
2. **The compiler**, site by site, one commit per file group (`project_drive.nika`, then the rest): join for read_dir names, guards where a component is meant, the D15 line where the tool opens what it is given. Each change built with `nikaia lower-std` and the touched tests run.
3. **`scripts/`**: `drive.nika`, `agent.nika` and the rest; `mktemp` to `fs::scratch()` where a scratch root fits, else `fs::scratch().path()` (a method on its value, #2336); the script's own D15 line if it is a package with a manifest. One commit per script or group.
4. **`examples/` and `packages/`**: the 14 sites; a package that reads a path from its user gets its own D15 line with a comment.
5. **The report** lists each site no proof and no D15 line covers as `Found:` with file, line and what it would need.

## Files and limits

`crates/nikaia-std/src/compiler/*.nika` and their lowered files, `scripts/*.nika`, `examples/**`, `packages/**`, the manifests that get a D15 line, the one test above. Not `tests/compiler/tests/` (the test migration issue), not `std` (the std issue), not the check itself (`project_check_let_raw_sinks_through`, `prover_raw_sink`). No new Rust. Each D15 line is as narrow as the site needs: `-read` before `-anywhere`, a source list before `true`.

## Ruled out

* `trusted:` at sites: rejected by the owner on #2242 as boilerplate and dangerous (D16).
* `fs::exists` / `fs::metadata` checks as proof: they hold for the moment of the call (D14).
* `untrusted-paths-anywhere = true` for the whole compiler: the compiler writes and removes in its cache, where a path from outside must not reach.

# Issue #2379: A program counts its allocations only where it reads the counts or sets a budget

[Open and answer this issue on GitHub](https://github.com/Nikaia-Foundation/Nikaia/issues/2379).

`runtime`, `performance`, `decision` · opened 2026-11-20 · updated 2026-11-20 · 0 comments

Found while a Counting global allocator in the nikaia binary costs +4.2 % instructions (#2368)
Part of std::mem: allocations() and usage() per thread (ADR-400) (#2112)

## Goal
A program pays for counting its allocations only where it reads the counts. Today every emitted program and (with #2368) the `nikaia` binary installs `task_block::Counting` (`crates/unsafe/task-block/src/lib.rs`), which on every `alloc`, `dealloc` and `realloc` adds to the thread's `TALLY` (ADR-400 D1, D2) and to the running block's `outside` (ADR-327 D9, D10).

## Measured (callgrind, a compile of `tests/compiler/tests/byteset_every_search_is_the_byte_by_byte_one.nika`)
* system allocator: 4,439,441,817 Ir; Counting: 4,608,631,081 Ir (+3.81 %).
* about 6.05 M alloc, 6.04 M dealloc and 0.88 M realloc calls: about 13 Ir per call. `__rust_alloc` grows from a jump to `malloc` to a framed function with two thread-local updates (the TLS reads are already direct `%fs` offsets, no `__tls_get_addr`).

## To decide
* Who needs the counts: a program that calls `std::mem::allocations()` / `usage()`, a test block that does, and a task with a memory budget (ADR-327 D15 reads `outside`).
* Options: (a) the compiler installs `Counting` only where the program (its closure of called functions) reaches `mem::allocations`, `mem::usage` or a budget, the system allocator otherwise; (b) one allocator with a counting switch read per call (cheaper, not free); (c) keep counting always and make it cheaper (one thread-local, count before the call so `malloc` is a tail call).
* Recommendation: (a), with (c)'s cheaper path for programs that count.

## Done when
A program that reads no counts and sets no budget runs with the system allocator (instruction count equal to it, measured), and one that reads them still gets ADR-400's numbers (`tests/compiler/tests/` test).

# Issue #2383: Rethink how programs get, reuse and free memory (arenas, pools, reuse, deferred frees), measured

[Open and answer this issue on GitHub](https://github.com/Nikaia-Foundation/Nikaia/issues/2383).

`runtime`, `performance`, `decision` · opened 2026-11-20 · updated 2026-11-20 · 0 comments

Found while a Counting global allocator in the nikaia binary costs +4.2 % instructions (#2368)
Related: Choosing the allocator: a build, a task or a call names where memory comes from, and an allocation that may fail returns a value (#1493); ADR-327 D4-D11: memory budgets per task and per shared value (#490)

## Goal
Rethink how Nikaia programs get, reuse and give back memory, beyond allocating less (the issue on the compiler allocating less). About 31 % of a compile's instructions are glibc's `malloc`/`free`; a task's block (ADR-327) already bump-allocates inside a segment, and everything outside it goes to the system allocator.

## To find out (a study, measured)
* Where values live: which allocations could go into the task's block, an arena per phase, or a pool per size, freed all at once at its end instead of one by one.
* Reuse: buffers and lists cleared and kept instead of dropped and allocated again; what the language could say about it (ownership already knows the last use).
* Freeing: frees deferred to the end of a block or phase; `malloc_consolidate` (67 M Ir in the compile above) points at fragmentation.
* Other allocators (a size-class allocator in place of glibc), measured against the same compile.

## Done when
A decision paper (options with measured figures, a recommendation) is attached here and the chosen steps are filed as issues.

# Issue #2385: The compiler warns where a program allocates without need: a buffer made anew each loop turn, text formatted only to be compared, a list grown one by one to a known length

[Open and answer this issue on GitHub](https://github.com/Nikaia-Foundation/Nikaia/issues/2385).

`compiler`, `diagnostics`, `performance`, `ready` · opened 2026-11-20 · updated 2026-11-20 · 9 comments

Found while: The compiler allocates less: glibc malloc/free take about 31 % of a compile's instructions (#2382)
Related: The checker warns on a `.clone()` that copies nothing new (#1318, done); Warn on a collect that only re-reads what a view already offers (#1932); Rethink how programs get, reuse and free memory (#2383)
Input: the list of the largest allocation sites from #2382 step 1 (done 2026-11-20, in the run report's comment on #2382)

## Goal
A program, ours first, is told where it allocates without need, so that the 6 M allocations of one compile do not come back after #2382 removes them. Today only a needless `.clone()` (#1318) and, once decided, a needless collect (#1932) are warned; the patterns behind the allocator's 31 % are not.

## To build
1. From #2382's list of sites, sort each by the pattern in the source that made it allocate. Candidates:
   * a `List`/`Text` made anew in each loop turn and dropped at its end, where one made before the loop and cleared would do (ownership knows the last use);
   * text built by formatting only to be compared, hashed, looked up or written at once;
   * a list grown one push at a time to a length known before the loop (one allocation of that size instead of log2(n) grows);
   * a map keyed by `Text` built from a slice that already lives as long as the map.
2. For each pattern that covers a large site and can be seen in the checker without false warnings: a warning with a code from the block the supervisor reserves, a test (`.nika` + `.stderr`) and the fix in the compiler's `.nika` source it finds.
3. Where the compiler can do the better thing itself without changing behaviour (reserve the known length, reuse the buffer), it does so instead of warning, and the report says which.
4. A pattern judged not worth a warning is recorded with its reason here.

## Done when
Each pattern of #2382's ten largest sites is warned, done by the compiler itself, or recorded as not worth it; the compiler's own source builds without these warnings.

## Comments

# Issue #2396: The bounds walk over the solver's simplex unit: rule checks are keyed on the held ids, so 288 of 561 walks never reuse an entry

[Open and answer this issue on GitHub](https://github.com/Nikaia-Foundation/Nikaia/issues/2396).

`ready`, `solver` · opened 2026-11-20 · updated 2026-11-21 · 8 comments

Part of "A cold build of scripts/solver.nika takes four minutes" (#1949), from the `Found:` of its run (fc26ca93).

## Found

`bounds_proven` over `packages/logic/src/sv_simplex.nika` cost 209.5 G Ir (callgrind, `--toggle-collect='nikaia::bounds::proven_traced*'` of `nikaia check src/sv_simplex.nika` in packages/logic).

**Run 1 (d10edda5)**: memoized `rules_check` in `Around.checked`. 209.5 G → 152.0 G.

**Run 2 (c49cc932)**: each entry keeps the field keys its walk asked `assumed` for (`fields`, `absent`); `rules_checked_keep` drops only stale entries. 156.4 G → 144.4 G.

**Run 3 (32622162)**: `rules_given_key` no longer holds `context.owner`; `BoundsWalk.self_read` records the `context.ensured` key each `self.m(...)` found under the owner (ADR-359 D14), `RulesChecked.selves` keeps it. Walks 740 → 561; 144.4 G → 127.9 G.

Of the 561 walks left:
- 288 are distinct keys driven by the held ids (72 without ids).
- 49 are re-misses after a stale drop.
- 224 are `bounds_returns` repeats with changed `context.returns`: that part is "bounds_returns runs 54 G of the bounds walk over the solver's simplex unit" (#2464).

The held ids cannot simply leave the key: `walk.rules` is read in about 18 places (`rules_give` among them, under the 48-fact cap), so the results depend on them.

**Supervisor decision (2026-11-21)**: the held ids are keyed by the held rules the walk read, recorded per entry the way `fields`/`absent` and `selves` are: the key holds no ids; an entry records which held rules (by their content, not their id) each read of `walk.rules` saw, including the cap cut, and is served only to a walk whose held rules give the same reads. This changes no verdict, only reuse.

## To build

- [x] Find where the cost goes (run 1).
- [x] Memoize `rules_check` across the rounds (run 1).
- [x] Narrow the drop to the field bounds each walk read, with a test (run 2).
- [x] Drop `context.owner` from the key; record what calls on self read (run 3).
- [ ] Record per entry the held rules each read of `walk.rules` saw (by content, with the 48-fact cut), drop the held ids from `rules_given_key`, serve an entry only where the same reads come out.
- [ ] Add a test in `tests/compiler/tests/`: two walks with different held ids but the same held rules read reuse one entry, and a walk whose held rules differ in what is read keeps its own verdict.

## Done when

- Waits for #2464 (built first; then measure again on its develop).
- Rule-check walks on sv_simplex at most 300 (debug count in the report).
- `bounds_proven` below 120 G (callgrind, same toggle).
- `nikaia check --bounds` gives identical results, old vs new binary, on `packages/logic` and on every `.bounds` test.

# Issue #2407: An empty /nikaia.toml makes `nikaia run` take / as the project; the stream tests guess the repo through the grandparent process

[Open and answer this issue on GitHub](https://github.com/Nikaia-Foundation/Nikaia/issues/2407).

`ready`, `bugs` · opened 2026-11-20 · updated 2026-11-20 · 0 comments

## Found

On 2026-11-20 at 07:38:16 UTC an empty `/nikaia.toml` (0 bytes, created, never written) appeared in a session container. It appeared during `nikaia test --filter stream`, in the same second the temp dir of `a_rust_library_reads_a_stream_entry` was made. From then on:

- `nikaia run scripts/drive.nika -- docs/briefs/yaml` failed with "scripts/drive.nika is not the entry point of the project at /."
- `nikaia run scripts/pre-push.nika` failed the same way.

The repository has no root `nikaia.toml`, so per ADR-260 D4 a script there is built as its own project. The upward manifest search instead stops at the empty `/nikaia.toml`.

**Suspected cause (not traced to a line):** the stream tests' `root()` (e.g. tests/compiler/tests/a_rust_library_reads_a_stream_entry.nika:20) guesses the repository from the cwd of the grandparent process, via `/proc/$PPID/stat`. When that process has already exited, PID 1 adopts the child, its cwd is `/`, and the guess becomes repo = `/`. A file written relative to the repository then lands in `/`.

## To build

- [ ] Tests do not guess the repository through `/proc/$PPID`: `nikaia test` hands the program the repository root and the toolchain (e.g. an environment variable), and the tests read that instead.
- [ ] The project lookup of `nikaia run` / `nikaia build` refuses, or skips with a warning, an empty `nikaia.toml` that names no package. A test in `tests/compiler/tests/` covers it.
- [ ] Find the line that created the file (run the 16 stream tests with `strace -f -e trace=openat` or equivalent) and name it in the commit.

## Done when

An empty manifest in a directory above a script no longer makes `nikaia run` refuse the script, with a test showing it, and no test reads `/proc/$PPID` to find the repository.

# Issue #2417: yaml: events and nodes refer to their scalars in the input instead of copying each into a String

[Open and answer this issue on GitHub](https://github.com/Nikaia-Foundation/Nikaia/issues/2417).

`blocked`, `yaml` · opened 2026-11-20 · updated 2026-11-20 · 6 comments

Filed by the supervisor (owner's goal, 2026-11-20: yaml faster than saphyr-parser).

Part of #1548.

## Goal

An event and a tree node hold their text as a view of the input instead of an owned `String`. Then a scalar costs no allocation and no copy between the parse and the walk.

## Today

- `pub struct Event` in packages/yaml/src/main.nika holds `value: String`, `text: String?`, `anchor: String?` and `tag: String?`. `walk` fills them from the `Node` tree, which holds its own `String` per scalar.
- So each scalar is allocated at least twice: once in the node, once in its event.
- `benches/yaml/README.md`, *Where yaml is behind*: `malloc` and `free` are about 11 % of `deep` with checks off (callgrind on `target/yaml-bench/bin/events.off`).

## To build

- [ ] Measure first: callgrind on `events.off` with `deep` and `large` at today's `develop`. Report the inclusive share of `malloc`/`free`/`memcpy` and how much of it comes from scalar strings.
- [ ] Check what ADR-views-v4 allows: can a `pub struct` returned from a package hold a view of the caller's input (`from`, a lent field)? Can the `@stream` entry's emitted items do the same?
  - Where the language allows neither, stop: `Result: blocked`, `Found:` with a probe of a few lines, `Needs: supervisor decision`.
- [ ] Build the views:
  - A plain or quoted scalar without escapes or folding refers to its bytes in the input.
  - Only a scalar whose value differs from its source text (escapes, folding, block chomping) owns a `String`.
- [ ] Re-run `nikaia run benches/yaml/bench.nika` and update the table in `benches/yaml/README.md`.

## Done when

- Events and nodes take no `String` for a scalar whose value is its source text.
- `events.off` counts fewer instructions on `deep`, `large` and `scalars` (figures from callgrind in the commit message).
- Outputs stay byte-identical. The package's tests and the yaml-test-suite pass list are green.

# Issue #2419: winnow-grammar picks an alternative by the first byte where the alternatives' first bytes are disjoint

[Open and answer this issue on GitHub](https://github.com/Nikaia-Foundation/Nikaia/issues/2419).

`wip`, `yaml` · opened 2026-11-20 · updated 2026-11-20 · 1 comment

Filed by the supervisor (owner's goal, 2026-11-20: yaml faster than saphyr-parser).

Part of #1548.

## Goal

winnow-grammar picks an alternative by the input's first byte where the alternatives' first bytes do not overlap, instead of trying them in turn. This helps every grammar written in Nikaia. Built in winnow-grammar (keywan-ghadami/winnow-grammar) and pinned in Nikaia, as for #2293.

## Today

- `benches/yaml/README.md`, *Where yaml is behind*: the choices of `FlowItem` and `FlowAny` and `winnow_grammar::rt::expected` are 15 % of `deep` (callgrind, `events.off`, checks off).
- winnow-grammar already has `rt::first_byte` for some alternatives: it appears in the profile of `MapEntry`.
- Which alternatives it does not cover, and why, is not known yet.

## To build

- [ ] Measure first: with callgrind on `events.off deep` and `large`, list the alternatives of the yaml grammar by inclusive cost. Note which of them `first_byte` covers in the generated code (winnow-grammar-macros, codegen of alternatives).
- [ ] In winnow-grammar, widen the first-byte dispatch:
  - to alternatives whose first sets are known after optional or trivia elements;
  - to sets of more than one byte (a 256-entry table);
  - with a fallback that tries in turn where the sets overlap.
  - Messages must stay byte-identical (ADR 17: the dispatch is a fast-pass decision; the diagnosing pass may keep trying in turn).
- [ ] winnow-grammar's tests green, `examples/stream_profile.rs` and a yaml profile measured; PR on winnow-grammar.
- [ ] Pin Nikaia to it (both `Cargo.toml` and both lock files); re-run `benches/yaml/bench.nika` and update the README table.

## Done when

- The alternatives of `FlowItem`, `FlowAny` and `Block` dispatch by first byte where their first sets are disjoint.
- `events.off deep` counts fewer instructions.
- All winnow-grammar and Nikaia tests are green, and the outputs are byte-identical.

### keywan-ghadami, [2026-11-20](https://github.com/Nikaia-Foundation/Nikaia/issues/2419#issuecomment-7042114440)

First measurement (supervisor session, winnow-grammar branch `first-bytes-fixpoint`, commits 1cf41ae and f15a5ed). Result: **no gain for yaml**.

**What the branch builds.** The first-byte sets in `first_bytes.rs` now reach almost every rule of the yaml grammar:
- Rules with value parameters get a set; before, a rule with any parameter got none.
- A pattern argument is put in place of its parameter (`__nikaia_count(p = " ")`).
- `count`, `empty`, `eof`, `any`, `text`, `bytes` and `span` are handled.
- `peek(p)` fixes the byte, so a cut after it no longer blocks the set (`SeqLevel`, `MapLevel`).
- The sets are a least fixed point, so a recursive rule (a node inside a node) gets a set instead of none.

winnow-grammar's tests stay 511/511, with new unit tests.

**Measured with callgrind** on `events.off` (opt 3, lto, checks off). Outputs are byte-identical:

| Input | Before | After |
| :--- | ---: | ---: |
| deep | 140.61M | 140.45M |
| scalars | 210.82M | 211.86M |
| large | 4,494.95M | 4,500.53M |

**Why it does not help.** The costly alternatives (`Block`, `Content`, `Inline`, `FlowItem`, `FlowAny`, `FlowNode`, `KeyNode`) reach a plain scalar early. A plain scalar begins with `x:any if(plain_safe(...))`, and its first set is every byte, so their sets are full and no guard is written. Where a set is narrow (`Seq`'s `-`, `KeyTail`), the guard costs about what it saves.

The two commits are reverted on the PR branch (keywan-ghadami/winnow-grammar#39, 15047c5) and kept on `first-bytes-fixpoint` for a grammar where they help.

**Where the 15 % of the alternatives does lie.** The alternatives repeat work they share:
- `Block`'s three alternatives each run `not(Marker) m:__nikaia_count(p = " ")` again before their guard.
- `Content` and `Spaced` each try `Seq`, `Map`, `Propped` and so on, which read the same properties and indentation.

Two directions follow:
- **(a) In the grammar.** Each rule reads the shared prefix once, as "packages/yaml counts each line's indentation twice" (#2411) does for `Blanks`/`Block`.
- **(b) In winnow-grammar.** The engine factors out a leading sequence that the alternatives of a rule share verbatim, with the same bindings, and parses it once.

I'll measure (b) next on the profile: how much of `Block`, `Content` and `Inline` is the repeated prefix. This issue stays `wip`.

# Issue #2425: A mut parameter may receive views of another parameter, inferred (ADR-views-v4 D32)

[Open and answer this issue on GitHub](https://github.com/Nikaia-Foundation/Nikaia/issues/2425).

`ready`, `yaml` · opened 2026-11-20 · updated 2026-11-21 · 4 comments

Filed by the driver from the `Found:` of the run of `issue-2417` (#2417). Decided by the owner on 2026-11-21 and recorded as ADR-views-v4 D32 (38ad2cf3).

Part of #1548.
Needs #2478

## Decision

A function may put a view of another lent parameter into a `mut` parameter: an element pushed, a field set, a value inserted. It may already hand one back as its result (D8).
- The source is **inferred** from the body, as for a result. Nothing is written at the parameter or at the call.
- `from` is written only where there is no body: a trait's method, a function type, a foreign or Rust function (D14's places). The form is `fn(n: Node, mut out: Vec[Event] from n)`.
- The caller treats the argument passed for `n` as D9 treats an argument a result views, for as long as what it passed for the `mut` parameter lives. It may give the argument up, but may not change it or hand it over.
- A `mut` parameter is no longer inferred `keep` because the body stores such a view.

## Probe (today)

```nika
struct N {
	raw: String,
}
struct E {
	v: String,
}
fn walk(n: N, mut out: Vec[E]) {
```
